desc: Build adjacency list, root the tree at node 1, and produce a post-order traversal iteratively to avoid recursion limit issues.
Define DP returning a pair `(size, has_hub)`. Use `( -inf, False )` as sentinel. For each child `ci`, contribution = `(dp1[ci].size + 1, dp1[ci].has_hub)`.
Compute for each node u: `best1` = max single contribution, `best3` = sum of top 3 contributions, `best4` = sum of top 4 contributions, tracking aggregated has_hub as any chosen has_hub.
`dp0[u]` = best4 (if at least 4 children with valid contributions) else `(0, False)`. `has_hub` = aggregated has_hub from best4.
`dp1[u]` = max between `(1, False)` (leaf option) and `best3` (hub option). `has_hub` = best3.has_hub if best3 is chosen, else False.
Post-process root r: consider dp0[r] and all children's dp0[c] to capture alkanes entirely within subtrees. Valid iff size >= 5 and has_hub == True. Output max size, or -1 if none.
Validate against all three sample cases (expected outputs: 8, -1, 11).
Consider edge cases: N=5 with a star (center degree 4), linear chain, etc.
Finalize and output the corrected solution.
